sections.heading: The API drift firewall for AI agents
sections.text: Keep AI agents working safely when the APIs they depend on change. Runtime protection for agent API writes: wrap the tool call, inspect request and response evidence, freeze a mode for that call, and keep the upstream result unless a verified selective repair or policy refusal applies. This is in-path write protection with evidence — not a standalone detection utility. Selective repair is a second, explicitly configured capability. Shape drift that would reject upstream can pass through or refuse under policy; semantic drift that would return wrong data must not invent a write. Local SDKs and execution hosts exist. The default engine detects nothing until explicitly configured. Production protection and hosted delivery remain unqualified.

sections.heading: Modes and decisions
sections.text: A mode (observe, repair, or strict) is configuration resolved before the call runs and frozen through completion—later configure updates cannot rewrite that call. A decision (ok, repaired, degraded, bypassed, or blocked) is only what that call produced. The two closed sets are not interchangeable; the full matrix lives on Modes.

sections.heading: Scope and limits
sections.text: AGINDOW is not a vendor credential manager or a promise that every write is correct. Findings, verified patches and metered incidents carry different evidence. The current default guest has no selective repair output. Audit delivery needs an explicit host sink and local queues can be lost. Durable replay and hosted delivery are unavailable.

sections.heading: Evaluate what works today
sections.text: Published pre-alpha packages on npm and PyPI do not imply production protection. Installing the SDK alone does not detect drift. Use the homepage capability evaluation matrix for local detection, SDK runtimes, repair seams, production boundaries and reproducible test links, open the browser playground for a labelled Unit finding without installing, then follow Quickstart for the install path.

sections.heading: Specification
sections.text: Read the published modes guide and the guard loop.

sections.heading: Install from the registries
sections.text: `Node 22+` and `Python 3.11+` are supported. Install the published pre-alpha packages with `npm install agindow@0.1.0-alpha.1` or `pip install agindow==0.1.0a0`. No hosted key is required. Installing the SDK alone does not detect drift. Configure a detector with baseline/live data windows. Monorepo contributors still build the shared WASM guest with the Rust target and `wasm-bindgen` CLI `0.2.129` when changing the engine. See Modes for the separate detector and mode setup requirements.

sections.heading: Detect a labelled simulated change
sections.text: After `npm install agindow@0.1.0-alpha.1`, save the TypeScript sample below as `detect.mts` and run `node --experimental-strip-types detect.mts`. Prerequisites: `Node.js 22+`, a clean directory, and network access only to install the published package — no monorepo, Rust/WASM toolchain, hosted keys, vendor credentials, live vendor traffic or paid services. The sample selects an explicit statistical window, awaits readiness, and reports a real Unit finding for a labelled numeric magnitude shift (baseline value `1` → live value `100`). An otherwise identical unchanged live window, a default engine with no selection, and insufficient windows report no detection. The printed JSON is the stable finding summary; `latencyUs` and host timing vary. This is observe-mode detection evidence, not an applied repair, not a bypass event, and not evidence of production accuracy.

sections.heading: Availability and identity fixtures
sections.text: The separately labelled ts/py examples below run a synthetic local read and an explicitly unavailable or closed-engine fixture. They assert return identity and one bypass event. They are availability fixtures, not detection. Use the language tab that matches your install, then run the sample with `node --experimental-strip-types example.ts` or `python example.py`.

sections.heading: Read the first outcome
sections.text: Inspect `sdk.recent()` or subscribe with `sdk.on`. A drift event with findings is detection evidence; bypass is an availability event and leaves the result body unchanged. A healthy default engine can return no findings without proving drift safety. Audit artifact production requires explicit audit options and a host drain; missing artifact IDs must stay unavailable.

import asyncio
from agindow import Agindow
sdk = Agindow(mode="observe")
payload = {"id": "synthetic-customer"}
@sdk.guard(tool="vendor.read", operation="read")
def read() -> dict[str, str]:
    return payload
@sdk.guard(tool="vendor.read", operation="read")
async def read_async() -> dict[str, str]:
    return payload
with sdk.context(mode="observe"):
    assert read() is payload
async def main() -> None:
    async with sdk.context(mode="observe"):
        assert await read_async() is payload
asyncio.run(main())
# A closed engine is a labelled availability fixture, not vendor drift.
sdk.close()
assert read() is payload
assert len([event for event in sdk.recent() if event.type == "bypass"]) == 1
print("Synthetic fixture: sync/async identity retained; closed engine bypassed once.")

sections.heading: What this is
sections.text: The public `/try` page runs labelled detection and a static source inventory in your browser tab. It uses the same guest WASM bytes as the published SDK for fixture detection. Files stay in the tab. Nothing is uploaded to AGINDOW servers. This is observe-mode detection evidence and non-authoritative scan output — not production protection and not an applied repair.

sections.heading: 1. Run the labelled sample
sections.text: On `/try`, under Fixture detection, click Run sample. The page loads the guest WASM only when you run. Expect two panels: Changed window (sample) shows a finding for the labelled numeric magnitude shift (baseline value `1` → live value `100`), typically with detector Unit and class semantic; Unchanged window (control) shows no drift. Status text may briefly say the guest is loading. Timing and `latencyUs` can vary; the finding fields are the stable evidence.

sections.heading: 2. Optional custom fixtures
sections.text: Caps: at most 5 text/JSON files, ≤256 KiB each, ≤1024 KiB total. Use Choose fixtures then Run fixtures, or paste fixture JSON into the textarea and run. Binaries, oversize sets and a sixth file are rejected. A result that mentions repair or block is dry-run only — proposed, not applied; no upstream call. The default guest has no selective repair output.

sections.heading: 3. Scan source inventory
sections.text: Under Source inventory, paste source in the TypeScript or Python tab (docs-style token colors — not IntelliSense) or Choose source files, then click Scan source. Inventory parses TypeScript/JavaScript only; a Python-only paste explains that limit and points to Quickstart for Python detection. This path does not load the guest WASM; it loads a separate scanner chunk in-tab. Expect a Scan summary with tools detected, wrap call sites (hint only), vendors and skipped files. Wrap hints never mean protection is on, writes are guarded, or config is effective. A static scan alone never grants protection.

sections.heading: 4. What not to expect
sections.text: No code execution of your paste beyond the static inventory parse, no registry snapshot, no applied selective repair, no vendor credentials, and no hosted write protection. Installing the SDK alone also does not detect drift — configure a detector with baseline/live windows after you leave the playground.

sections.heading: 5. Install and detect
sections.text: When you are ready to run the same labelled detection outside the browser, follow Quickstart for the pinned npm/PyPI install and the Node detect sample.

sections.heading: Local OSS
sections.text: Embedded Node and Python execution is key-free. Adding a key or endpoint configuration does not activate a hosted transport. Explicit remote execution is a separate API.

sections.heading: Dashboard sessions
sections.text: Browser sessions identify a user and authoritative organization membership. Local login forms exist; hosted login depends on host identity and mail configuration.

sections.heading: Customer API keys
sections.text: Customer fallback keys are organization/environment scoped credentials with separate lifecycle controls. Public issuance and production scope admission are unavailable. They are not browser sessions or upstream provider credentials.

sections.heading: Keyless machine authentication
sections.text: Opt-in local token/proof and workload identity exchange interfaces exist. Keys and registrations refresh outside tool calls. Replay and rate state are process-local; live identity-provider and hosted qualification are unavailable.

sections.heading: Producer secrets
sections.text: Third-party API credentials belong in explicit host connection bindings. Never place provider secrets in model context, tool arguments or public docs. A connection handle selects an authorized binding; it is not a credential.

sections.heading: Specification
sections.text: Read the published modes guide and the guard loop.

sections.heading: Availability gate
sections.text: Infrastructure fault → transparent bypass, loudly, once per call. Warming, engine faults and unavailable inspection preserve original results and exceptions in every mode. Internal faults never become policy refusals. A bypass event is emitted once per call, not once per phase.

sections.heading: Policy is separate
sections.text: Known policy rejection remains a rejection: blocked is distinct from bypassed. Reads with incomplete policy repair can be degraded; strict is an explicit policy escalation. An HTTP 5xx from an explicit remote guard invokes the documented fallback, subject to upstream-enforced idempotency for writes.

sections.heading: Uncertain or completed writes
sections.text: Inspect a retained completed outcome before deciding what to do next. Do not blindly replay a write with an uncertain outcome. Local replay state is not durable or distributed. Use the same upstream-enforced idempotency key in a remote request and its fallback; never generate a fresh key to repeat an uncertain write.

sections.heading: Specification
sections.text: Read the published modes guide and the guard loop.

sections.heading: Configure detection separately from mode
sections.text: The default engine passes calls through without detecting drift. Statistical detection requires an explicitly selected detector and baseline/live data windows. Observe controls how findings are handled: it records findings without applying repairs or policy blocks. Selecting observe mode does not configure a detector. Wait for detector readiness before relying on findings.

sections.heading: Mode matrix
sections.text: Choose observe, repair or strict explicitly. SDK default is observe with the no-op engine, which detects nothing. Configuration resolves explicit values over environment over the nearest JSON configuration over defaults. Guard options and later configure updates apply to future calls; an executing call retains its frozen configuration.

rows: Log and audit only; preserves upstream outcomes.
Reads fail open with degraded; semantic writes fail closed. Shape/unknown writes default fail closed, with explicit failClosed opt-out; malformed whole bodies pass through without repair.
Incomplete repair fails closed; confidence below 0.99 halts for review. Ignores failClosed opt-out. Infrastructure failures still bypass.

sections.heading: Per-call decisions
sections.text: Mode names are not outcome names. The status header and audit decision use exactly these five values.

rows: No actionable drift reported; this alone does not prove protection was configured.
A verified selective patch was applied; bytes may change and byte_identical is false.
Policy permits the original read with a loud drift warning.
Inspection unavailable or skipped; original outcome preserved.
Policy refusal; distinguish request refusal from a completed response halt.

sections.heading: Classification and repair metadata
sections.text: Drift classes are shape, semantic and unknown. Repair header values are applied, skipped and failed. Wrapper events are drift, repair, blocked, bypass and error. An event name does not replace the status enum. Observe never applies a candidate replacement. Semantic writes cannot opt out of protection in repair mode.

sections.heading: Interpret evidence
sections.text: A unit test does not establish latency. A report must identify runtime, hardware, build, workload and included costs. There is no hosted latency or uptime guarantee. Registry refresh runs asynchronously outside the call path.

sections.heading: Specification
sections.text: Read the published modes guide and the guard loop.

sections.heading: Wrap → inspect → decision → audit → feedback
sections.text: Wrap the callable. Inspect bounded complete request and response evidence before dispatch and after a response. Supplied OpenAPI, schema or contract evidence and runtime failures are inputs; they are not themselves detection. Freeze the mode for both phases. Produce ok / repaired / degraded / bypassed / blocked. Export an audit artifact through an explicitly configured sink. Optional feedback informs later investigation; it cannot authorize replay or change a completed decision. Response inspection cannot undo a completed upstream write; availability faults bypass inspection even for writes.

sections.heading: Evidence classes
sections.text: A finding describes drift evidence. A patch describes a proposed or verified selective change. An incident is a separately admitted accounting unit. A candidate is not an applied repair; an audit artifact is not automatically write-integrity proof. Incomplete captures are unavailable evidence, not malformed vendor bodies.

sections.heading: Rename authority versus meaning
sections.text: A fictional mechanical rename (for example order_ref → order_id) may be considered only with authoritative migration facts, independent verification of the migration constraint, sufficient confidence and preservation of untouched caller fields. Schema acceptance and confidence alone are insufficient to establish intent or persisted write correctness. An ambiguous source ↔ payment_method mapping cannot establish intended meaning from matching names or types; it is not a verified real payment-provider migration. Observe records without changing the call; repair mode blocks unresolved semantic write drift. Human review is an explicit host integration — a review receipt does not execute or replay the write.

sections.heading: Byte identity
sections.text: No-repair paths preserve original payload identity. Selective repair changes only verified drifted fields and records byte_identical: false. Numeric coercion is not a repair. The default guest supplies no selective repair output.

sections.heading: Specification
sections.text: Read the published modes guide and the guard loop.

sections.heading: Local adapter release matrix
sections.text: The Node package `agindow@0.1.0-alpha.1`, published on npm, supplies these adapters. Integration order is Pipedream → LangChain → Nango → Mastra. This order does not claim equal framework coverage or hosted partner adoption.

rows: Local clientAdapter(client.proxy); synthetic proxy transport fixture.
Local toolAdapter invoke and ToolCall fixture; batch/stream paths unqualified.
Local report and limited sandbox codegen; npm-forbidden sandboxes require codegen, not WASM installation.
Generic tool-shape adapter only where supported; dedicated framework qualification unavailable.

sections.heading: Choose the actual boundary
sections.text: Use `toolAdapter` for supported func/execute/invoke maps and arrays, `clientAdapter` for supported HTTP methods, and `httpAdapter` for Fetch/Express boundaries. Wrap selects a supported shape and refuses ambiguity before execution. Client storage and authentication helpers are not HTTP calls. Local SDK examples in the Node package exercise actual Pipedream proxy and LangChain tool executors without provider credentials.

sections.heading: Nango sandbox gate
sections.text: Use the separately validated report/codegen path for Nango sandboxes that forbid npm. Generated code has no credential lookups or imports. Only explicitly confirmed same-type request sibling renames are supported; deployed sandbox qualification remains unavailable.

sections.heading: Continue
sections.text: Keep configuration, call decisions and evidence separate.

sections.heading: Start with a read and observe
sections.text: Install the published SDK as described in Quickstart, select observe explicitly, await ready, and wrap the boundary you own. The validated synthetic example below retains the exact result object and never enables a repair path. The default engine passes calls through without detecting drift. Configure a statistical detector with scoped baseline/live data windows; selecting observe mode does not configure a detector.

sections.heading: Read candidates without applying them
sections.text: Subscribe with `sdk.on` to drift, repair, blocked, bypass and error events, or inspect `sdk.recent()`. A proposed patch is not an applied repair. The second snippet injects a labelled synthetic candidate engine and asserts that observe retains the original object even when a replacement is offered. Observe never mutates even when a trusted engine proposes a replacement. A bypass means inspection was unavailable; it is not clean drift evidence.

sections.heading: When to stay in observe
sections.text: Do not switch based on candidate count or recovery rate alone. Require representative baseline/live windows, scoped operation identities, verified patches and violation-rate evidence. Missing evidence, cold baselines and unsupported captures need investigation. The default guest has no selective repair output; changing mode cannot supply it. Semantic writes remain protected in repair mode; strict requires explicit review handling.

sections.text: Keep configuration, call decisions and evidence separate.

sections.heading: Runtime contract error taxonomy
sections.text: These are the contract §7 error names and HTTP statuses. This is the runtime specification, not a claim that the MCP endpoint implements the guard envelope.

rows: Bad envelope or missing write idempotency key.
Availability failure; explicit client fallback rules apply.

sections.heading: Five decisions
sections.text: Engine fault `bypassed` is different from policy `blocked`. A fail-open read can be `degraded`; a successful selective replacement is `repaired`.

rows: No actionable drift reported; this alone does not prove protection was configured.
A verified selective patch was applied; bytes may change and byte_identical is false.
Policy permits the original read with a loud drift warning.
Inspection unavailable or skipped; original outcome preserved.
Policy refusal; distinguish request refusal from a completed response halt.

sections.heading: SDK and administration errors
sections.text: `AgindowSetupError` is deterministic misuse before a call. `AgindowDriftError` carries policy feedback and preserves original exceptions as cause where available. A response halt may retain a completed outcome; inspect it before taking further action. Dashboard session, permissions, retention and validation failures belong to their own administrative contracts, not this runtime taxonomy.

sections.heading: Bypass
sections.text: Await Node `ready`; check Python `ready` and `load_error`. Confirm explicit detector selection, tool scope, complete captures and work allowance. A retired guest requires a new SDK instance. Inspect the bypass event; do not infer protection from unchanged output.

sections.heading: Blocked
sections.text: Read the structured drift hint, phase and retained outcome. Request refusal dispatches nothing; a response halt can follow a completed upstream write. Do not blindly replay it. Review classified evidence and upstream-enforced idempotency before any further write.

sections.heading: Retention expired
sections.text: Check the authoritative retention receipt or archive owner. Missing or expired evidence is unavailable; it is not proof of no drift. Local queues are bounded and may be lost on restart. Do not fabricate an artifact or reconstruct secret payloads from summaries.

sections.heading: Cold baseline
sections.text: Supply explicit comparable baseline/live windows in the supported scope. A warming or missing baseline cannot establish confidence. Keep observe until there is representative evidence; changing mode does not warm the baseline.

sections.heading: Unavailable adapter
sections.text: Check the local adapter matrix and use the explicit supported boundary. Unsupported shapes remain unchanged or produce a named setup refusal for ambiguity. Use Nango codegen only at its supported sandbox gate; a planned adapter has no install instructions.

sections.heading: Verify Ed25519 before use
sections.text: Fetch GET /openapi.json from your configured surface origin. Read x-agindow-signature, require algorithm Ed25519 and canonicalization agindow.canonical-json/1. Resolve key_id through an independently trusted public-key configuration. Remove x-agindow-signature from the document; recursively sort object keys, preserve array order and JSON primitives, and encode the canonical JSON as UTF-8. Decode the base64 signature and verify the exact bytes with the pinned Ed25519 key. Reject unknown key_id, algorithm or canonicalization and any verification failure. Never trust a key delivered beside the document. The signed tools inputSchema/outputSchema are included in those bytes.

sections.heading: Local interface preview
sections.text: AGINDOW is a pre-alpha API drift firewall. Installing the SDK alone does not detect drift. Coverage describes observed evidence and cannot prove every API change is safe. The local MCP interface exposes lookup_contract, query_drift, fetch_audit, simulate_repair and coverage_report. Requests require authorization; simulations never execute writes. A hosted endpoint is not available yet.

sections.heading: Runnable example
sections.text: For a configured local endpoint, set AGINDOW_SURFACE to its origin and AGINDOW_KEY to your authorized credential, then run the example below. No hosted endpoint or API key issuance is available yet.

sections.heading: Verify the API description
sections.text: Get /openapi.json and verify its x-agindow-signature with an independently trusted Ed25519 public key and key_id. Remove the signature field, encode using agindow.canonical-json/1 (recursively sorted keys, JSON primitives), then verify the exact UTF-8 bytes. The signed tools contain the input and output schemas served by MCP. Never trust a public key merely because the response includes it.

sections.heading: Version-pinned packages
sections.text: Pinned Node, Python and CLI versions are published on npm and PyPI. Install from the registries for application use; monorepo contributors still build the shared WASM guest when changing the engine. Examples are compiled/imported and executed against the built packages before documentation publication.

sections.heading: Install
sections.text: Install with `npm install agindow@0.1.0-alpha.1` or `pip install agindow==0.1.0a0`. CLI ships in the Node package as `agindow`. Installing the SDK alone does not detect drift. Configure a detector with baseline/live data windows.

sections.heading: Continue
sections.text: Published packages and local monorepo builds share the same APIs. Choose the transport explicitly.

sections.heading: Create and await ready
sections.text: `agindow@0.1.0-alpha.1`, published on npm. `Node 22+`, ESM/CJS and declarations. Engine contributors still need `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `wasm-bindgen` CLI `0.2.129` at build time. `createAgindow` returns an SDK instance. Await `sdk.ready`, a settling Promise; loading failure remains a bypass and does not become successful protection.

sections.heading: guard, wrap and adapters
sections.text: `sdk.guard(fn, options)` retains sync/async behavior, receiver, arguments, original exceptions and no-repair result identity. `sdk.wrap` selects a supported boundary. `sdk.toolAdapter`, `sdk.clientAdapter` and `sdk.httpAdapter` expose explicit adapters. Module exports `guard` and `wrap` use the default instance. HTTP streaming and framework batch paths have explicit capture limits; no universal framework adapter is implied.

sections.heading: configure and mode resolution
sections.text: `sdk.configure` changes later calls. Resolution at construction is explicit > environment > nearest JSON `.agindowrc` > defaults. Calls freeze configuration through completion. Default mode is `observe` and default engine is `NullEngine`: no detection or repair. Use `operation: write` or `unknown` explicitly for writes; generic callables default to read. Later configure updates can supersede existing guard options for future calls.

sections.heading: Events, audit and explicit remote API
sections.text: `sdk.on` returns an unsubscribe callback; `sdk.recent` returns bounded retained metadata. Optional audit requires explicit tenant options and `sdk.drainAudit` host delivery. `guardRemote` is a separate opt-in HTTP API, never the default guard. Write fallbacks require upstream-enforced idempotency. Default-guest selective repair, durable replay and hosted delivery remain unavailable.

sections.heading: Validated fixture
sections.text: Use the ts tab after `npm install agindow@0.1.0-alpha.1`, or the py tab after `pip install agindow==0.1.0a0`. The deliberate unavailable or closed-engine case is labelled synthetic, preserves identity and emits one bypass.

sections.heading: Continue
sections.text: Published packages and local monorepo builds share the same APIs. Choose the transport explicitly.

payload = {"id": "synthetic-customer"}
@sdk.guard(tool="vendor.read", operation="read")
def read() -> dict[str, str]:
    return payload
@sdk.guard(tool="vendor.read", operation="read")
async def read_async() -> dict[str, str]:
    return payload
with sdk.context(mode="observe"):
    assert read() is payload
async def main() -> None:
    async with sdk.context(mode="observe"):
        assert await read_async() is payload
asyncio.run(main())
# A closed engine is a labelled availability fixture, not vendor drift.
sdk.close()
assert read() is payload
assert len([event for event in sdk.recent() if event.type == "bypass"]) == 1
print("Synthetic fixture: sync/async identity retained; closed engine bypassed once.")

sections.heading: Shared WASM, separate Python host
sections.text: `agindow==0.1.0a0`, published on PyPI. `Python 3.11+`, pinned Wasmtime, and identical WASM bytes to Node. Install with `pip install agindow==0.1.0a0`. No separate Python detector or framework adapter is shipped.

sections.heading: Decorators and ContextVar scopes
sections.text: `Agindow.guard` works as a decorator; `wrap` accepts callables. `with sdk.context` and `async with sdk.context` apply ContextVar overrides only to that SDK’s guarded calls, remain isolated across tasks and freeze for call completion. Sync stays sync, async stays async, and cancellation propagates. The py tab validates both scopes and original object identity.

sections.heading: Readiness and configuration
sections.text: `sdk.ready` is a synchronous boolean after loading, unlike Node’s Promise; `sdk.load_error` retains failure. `configure` changes future calls. Snake_case keywords resolve explicit > environment > nearest JSON `.agindowrc` > defaults. `NullEngine` and `observe` are defaults. `sdk.close` releases the guest; later calls bypass.

sections.heading: Remote and framework boundaries
sections.text: `guard_remote` and `guard_remote_async` are explicit HTTP APIs, separate from local decorators. There are no Python framework adapters, built-in report CLI, distributed replay or hosted delivery. The shared default guest has no selective repair output.

sections.heading: Run the fixture
sections.text: Select the py tab, save as `example.py` after `pip install agindow==0.1.0a0`, then run `python example.py`. Sync, async and closed-engine outcomes are synthetic local evidence.

sections.heading: Offline report
sections.text: The CLI is bundled in the published Node `0.1.0-alpha.1` distribution (`npm install agindow@0.1.0-alpha.1`). After install, run `agindow report` against a path. `report` scans bounded static definitions and call sites without importing or executing project code, writing project files or contacting a provider. The installed binary is `agindow`.

sections.heading: Simulation and recordings
sections.text: `sdk.simulate(tool, input)` evaluates recorded payloads without calling upstream. It is an SDK method, not a CLI `simulate` subcommand. Await ready first. Partial or missing evidence is unavailable. Optional `report --snapshot` uses local frozen events and explicit sandbox recordings. Historical shape candidates do not authorize repairs.

sections.heading: Codegen is separate
sections.text: `codegen` emits the bounded sandbox evaluator. `scan` with an explicit `--snapshot` can modify supported Nango source forms, so it is distinct from the read-only report. Generation does not provision hosted refresh or qualify deployed integrations.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: A report is not write-integrity proof, production recovery evidence or permission to enable repair. Missing evidence is unavailable, not clean. The report cannot establish durable replay, complete framework coverage, streaming correctness or hosted readiness.
